title: Adyen (routed authorize) — PYC-40001 decline / HTTP 500 actually caused by wrong Adyen PSP credentials
symptom: Routed authorization through Adyen fails: the purchase returns PYC-40001 ('Payment was declined. Try another card or contact your bank.' / 'We are currently validating the status of your transaction...') with HTTP 500 instead of 200. The order never reaches the expected 'authorized' status, failing at the step 'It is validated that the order has been processed successfully with status authorized'. The error surfaces as a PSP decline / server error mapped from Adyen's routed authorization, but it is NOT a genuine card decline.
recipe: Misleading symptom: PYC-40001 + HTTP 500 looks like a real psp_decline, but the actual root cause here was WRONG/STALE Adyen PSP credentials used when configuring the processor. The fix was to update the credentials with which the Adyen PSP is configured (the credentials feeding `processorsConfig.adyenProcessorAuthorize` / `apiCallNewman.createPaymentProcessor`); once corrected, the routed authorization stopped returning the 500 / PYC-40001 and reached 'authorized'. Do NOT relax the assertion or swap the card as test data — verify the Adyen processor credentials are valid and current first. The prior --no-pr analysis suggested testDataFixer, but the real resolution was a credentials change.
